title: Compact Decomposition of Irregular Tensors for Data Compression: From Sparse to Dense to High-Order Tensors

problem.claim: Irregular tensors represent real-world data with varying lengths across matrices.

gap.claim: Existing irregular tensor decomposition methods have limited compression performance because they require a larger number of first-mode factor matrices.

contributions.claim: The analysis finds that irregular tensor decomposition methods have limited compression performance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that compression performance is limited by the larger number of first-mode factor matrices.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines an irregular tensor as a collection of matrices with different row counts.
Explains that varying data lengths make irregular tensors suitable representations for diverse real-world data.
Notes that tensor decomposition methods such as PARAFAC2 have been developed for analyzing irregular tensors.
Reports limited compression performance associated with the larger number of first-mode factor matrices.

source_observation.claim: Irregular tensor decomposition methods can have limited compression performance when they use more first-mode factor matrices.

interpretation.claim: The number of factor matrices is a relevant consideration when evaluating compression approaches for irregular tensors.

application.claim: Compression evaluations for irregular tensors should examine the effect of first-mode factor-matrix count.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish whether this limitation applies to every irregular tensor or decomposition setting.

unknowns: No proposed decomposition method is described.
No quantitative compression results are supplied.
No datasets, baselines, or experimental conditions are specified.
